name: FerrumPix 0.9.74-4
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.74


### Changes

- **Import from phones and cameras:** phones and cameras connected over USB now show up as
  sources in the import, each storage of a phone on its own. On KDE they are read through KDE's
  own device service, elsewhere through the desktop's device mounts. Every picture is still
  checked after copying.

- **Sharper thumbnails:** a new setting, "High resolution thumbnails", stores thumbnails twice as
  wide, so the largest gallery tiles no longer look soft. It needs more disk space and memory;
  switching it off again replaces them with the smaller ones.

- **Slideshow you can pause:** SPACE or the new button pauses the slideshow without leaving it.
  In fullscreen a small control bar appears when you move the mouse and stays while paused, with
  previous, pause, next, zoom and exit. While paused you can zoom in and drag the picture around.
  Touching the edge of the screen where the filmstrip is set to appear brings it up to jump to any
  picture.
  The bar also switches random order and the filmstrip on and off and sets how long each picture
  stays, and a bar at the top rates, marks as favourite, colour labels and keeps or rejects the
  picture on screen. Fullscreen without a running slideshow behaves the same way, as a paused
  slideshow ready to start. RAW files no longer leave a black screen
  between pictures: the next one is developed while the current one is on screen.

- **Mouse wheel your way:** the settings decide what the mouse wheel does, separately for the
  viewer and for fullscreen and slideshow: change the picture or zoom. Changing the picture is the
  default. With CTRL the wheel does the other, with the right mouse button held it always zooms.

- **Keyboard shortcuts on F1:** F1 opens the list of keyboard shortcuts from anywhere, also in
  fullscreen. It is the same list as in the settings, now including the slideshow and fullscreen
  keys.

- **Keep and reject next to the heart:** in the info panel, in every context and footer menu and
  on both sides of the viewer's comparison, two buttons next to the stars and the heart mark the
  pictures as kept (green) or rejected (red); pressing the same one again takes the mark back.
  The separate menu entry for rejecting is gone, and so is the small cross for clearing stars or
  colour labels, since clicking the same star or colour again already clears it.

- **New symbols:** the whole interface and the symbol gallery in the editor use a new, more even
  set of symbols. In the editor each symbol comes in five weights, from thin to filled, and inserted
  symbols draw cleanly with fill and outline. Symbols placed in pictures before keep their place;
  where the new set has no match they show a question mark and can be replaced.
  A frame made of symbols can now use any symbol of the gallery, in any of the five weights.

- **Converting a selection creates the layer:** the button that turns a selection into a mask or
  back now creates the matching layer right away. With a selection or mask layer picked in the
  layer panel, it converts that layer instead.

- **SVG graphics stay visible on dark tiles:** in the gallery and the filmstrips, SVG files now sit
  on a light background, so black outlines no longer disappear in the dark theme.

- **Filmstrip on any side:** in the settings the filmstrip can sit below, above, left or right of
  the picture, separately for the viewer, the editor and fullscreen. All filmstrip settings now
  have a section of their own.

### Fixes

- **Measured monitor profiles work:** monitor profiles made with a calibration device, for example
  with DisplayCAL, were refused as "not a readable ICC profile". They are read now, with their own
  curve for each colour channel.

- **Clicks no longer get lost under a tooltip:** buttons in the footers and the slideshow bar, and
  tiles when selecting in the gallery, sometimes ignored a click while their tooltip was showing.
  Tooltips now let clicks through.

- **Ratings show up everywhere at once:** stars, favourites and colour labels given in the viewer,
  the slideshow or the editor now appear right away on the gallery tiles, in the filmstrips and in
  the info panels.

- **Month names in your language:** folder and file name patterns with dates, in the import
  targets, batch rename and the editor's name suggestion, now write month and day names in the
  language of your region, for example "10 ottobre" instead of "10 October".

- **Slideshow timing after skipping by hand:** moving to another picture yourself now starts the
  full slideshow interval again, instead of showing the next picture after whatever was left of
  the old one.

- **Show the mask only stays on while painting:** brushing on a mask no longer switches back to
  the red overlay over the photo, so you can see exactly what is left to remove. Parts already
  brushed away no longer turn red again on the next stroke.

- **Large saved searches stay responsive:** while a saved search with many results fills the
  gallery, it no longer re-sorts everything after each small batch, so the window no longer
  stalls on very large collections.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.75-1
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.75


### Changes

- **New tool: Lighting.** Place lights and shadows anywhere on the picture and aim them right
  there: point light, spot with direction and cone, soft area light, grazing light and sun rays,
  each with brightness, reach, softness, color temperature or a free color and an optional halo.
  Light types like candle, bulb, LED, street lamp, floodlight, flashlight, evening sun, neon or
  shadow give a quick start. With the depth model the light can follow the depth of the scene. The
  lights stay editable at any time and are saved with the picture's edit. Lights now work like light
  at the time of the shot, before tone and colour, so bright light rolls off softly instead of
  clipping. A light can stand higher or lower above the scene, an ambient control darkens or
  brightens the scene around the lights, and with the depth model light follows the shape of
  surfaces and can cast shadows behind objects.

- **Faster import from large cards:** the capture days and all options appear right away, the
  exact capture data is read in the background afterwards.

- **Job name and file names on import:** a job like a photo trip, place or client can be entered
  in the import dialog and used as {job} in the target folder and the file name. The file name can
  be built from placeholders too, with the original name, capture date, camera and a counter that
  a RAW and its JPEG share. Like target folders, file name patterns can be defined in the settings
  and picked in the dialog.

- **Symbols found in every language:** the symbol search in the editor knows all symbols by name
  in every language of the app, and also finds them by related words, so "dog" finds the paw.

- **Shapes follow the symbol weight:** with "Filled" a new shape comes as a filled area, with thin
  to bold as an outline of matching width.

- **Bars hide when idle:** in fullscreen and in a paused slideshow the control bars and the mouse
  pointer now disappear after a moment without movement, just like while the slideshow plays.

### Fixes

- Lighting: a picture without an edit no longer shows the lights of the picture opened before it.
- Import: a target folder pattern is remembered for the next import. New placeholders {make} and
  {model} give the camera's make and model on their own, {camera} no longer repeats the make, and
  videos without camera information go to "Video" instead of "No camera".

- Import: when the import button is disabled, the summary now says why, for example a target
  outside the folders FerrumPix may write to, and where to allow it.

- Distort: the live preview of Grid and Warp now appears from the first drag, also at the
  corners, instead of only after a second handle was moved.

- Smaller close and clear crosses everywhere, and the frame switch next to the editor's zoom is
  gone; the frame is switched in its own group.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.73-4
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.73


### Changes

- **Dehaze works more like you would expect:** removing haze clears hazy pictures more strongly
  and gives them deeper blacks, while clear shadows stay protected. Adding haze now lays a veil
  that follows the picture, stronger in soft, bright areas and lighter on fine detail, instead of
  a flat grey wash.

- **Shadows and Highlights adapt better to each picture:** both sliders now look at the whole
  brightness distribution of the picture, not just its average brightness, and suit dark and
  bright pictures better. Used together, they now hold each other back a little, so lowering
  Highlights and lifting Shadows at the same time no longer overdoes it, for example on skin in
  dark stage photos. Lifted shadows also gain some colour instead of turning grey, and darkened
  shadows lose a little. Lowering Highlights no longer makes darkened midtones more colourful.

- **Tone curves keep colours more natural:** the main tone curve, including the parametric
  curve of presets, now changes brightness and contrast without twisting colours as much. Skin
  tones in particular stay warmer when a preset darkens the shadows. 

- **Similar pictures:** a new view in the gallery groups near duplicates of a folder, such as the
  shots of a series, with a sharpness bar on each picture and the sharpest one marked. Three levels
  decide how close the pictures have to be.

- **Keywords inside the file:** two new settings write the keywords you add into JPEG, PNG and WebP
  files themselves, as XMP, IPTC or both, when you add them and when you save or export. AI
  keywords are never written into files.

- **Import:** a new entry above Settings in the gallery sidebar copies pictures and videos from a
  memory card or any other folder, with or without its subfolders, into your collection, by
  shooting day, into the current folder or one of your own destinations. Destinations are set up
  in the settings and can use placeholders such as the year or day a picture was taken, or the
  camera. Every copy is checked against the original, nothing on the card is changed and nothing
  in the destination is replaced; pictures already there are skipped.

- **Backup and restore:** the catalogue, the Immich and Nextcloud indexes, the settings, favourites
  and saved searches can be backed up into a ZIP file from the settings and restored later, each
  part on its own. Server credentials only go in if you ask for it. Before a restore the current
  state is backed up, and the restore is applied the next time FerrumPix starts. Restoring on
  another computer can point the paths to where the photos are kept there.

- **Disconnected drives are safe in Clean database:** pictures on a drive that is not connected
  are no longer treated as deleted. Their ratings, keywords and people stay, and for each such
  drive you are asked whether to remove them anyway.

### Fixes

- The thumbnail memory cache now holds at least 1000 thumbnails. With a smaller cache, tiles in
  large folders could stay dark.

- HEIC photos from Huawei phones that were already in the gallery before 0.9.72 now show the
  camera under their tile too, not only in the info panel.
  
- Deleting inside an Immich or Nextcloud album now only removes the pictures from that album.
  They stay in your library on the server. Before, the picture was deleted from the whole library.
  The menu entry says "Remove from album", and it works even if deleting on the server is turned
  off in the settings.
  
- Selected text in input fields stays readable with a light accent colour such as yellow, for
  example the file name in Save as.
  
- The Save as dialog is wider, so the Carry over buttons and the destination folder fit again,
  and the line above the file name is no longer cut off with a larger font size.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.72-3
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.72


### Changes

- **Stronger luminance noise reduction with a working Detail slider:** the luminance noise
  reduction now smooths much more strongly at the same value; before, even 100 did little. The
  Detail slider now keeps fine texture such as hair and fabric
  while flat areas stay smooth, and it has a visible effect from about the middle of its range.
  Presets with a luminance value now look as intended. Pictures you already edited with luminance
  noise reduction come out smoother.

- **Dragging in the viewer moves the picture:** when you are zoomed in, dragging with the left
  mouse button now scrolls the picture instead of drawing a crop frame. If you liked the crop
  frame, turn on "Crop by dragging" in the viewer settings.

- **Faster colour noise reduction:** with colour noise reduction on, moving exposure, curves or
  colour sliders no longer redoes the noise reduction each time, and the noise reduction itself
  runs faster and on the graphics card when that is switched on.

- **Next picture after rating:** a new viewer setting moves on to the next picture as soon as you
  give it stars, so you can rate a whole folder with the number keys alone.

- **Colour mixer now acts before the curves:** in presets that use both, the
  colour mixer now acts before the curves, so the colour look the curves add stays as intended.
  The colour mixer also picks its colour ranges more precisely, so strong colours such as stage
  light react to the right slider, and lowering saturation also reaches muted colours.
  Turning the hue of a colour range now moves greens, blues, aquas and purples towards the
  colour you expect instead of a wrong neighbour, and saturation and luminance per range match
  presets more closely. Pictures you already edited with hue changes in the colour mixer may
  look slightly different.

- **Temperature and tint of RAW photos on the standard scale:** the numbers in the editor, in
  saved edits and in XMP presets now mean the same thing, so a preset
  with a green or magenta tint looks as intended. The tint shown for a photo "as shot" is now a
  small, familiar value. When you set a very different light, colours now shift the way the
  camera would have recorded them under that light, not just the white. Pictures you already
  edited keep their look; only the numbers shown for them change.

- **Shuffle the slideshow:** a new viewer setting plays the slideshow in random order. Every
  picture is shown once before the order is mixed again.

- **Crisper sharpening:** the Sharpening slider now brings out fine texture such as hair and
  fabric, without sharpening pixel noise more. Pictures you already sharpened come out a little crisper.

- **Liquify:** the Distort tool has a fifth mode with a brush that pushes, bloats, puckers,
  twirls, smooths or brings back the original. Like the other distortions it stays editable in
  the recipe, and masks and inserted objects move along.

- **Remove a plain background:** a photo or image layer on a plain background, such as a
  product shot on white, can have that background made transparent, for the photo from the
  right-click menu, for a layer from the layer menu. Soft edges stay soft, without a light fringe.
  For the photo, the result comes as a layer above it, the removed area is transparent, and the
  photo itself stays unchanged.

### Fixes

- **Presets with split toning and tone curves look as intended:** split toning in the shadows and
  highlights no longer brightens the picture, and presets that use both the parametric and the
  point curve keep more detail in the shadows.

- **Camera calibration looks as intended:** the hue and saturation sliders of the red, green and
  blue primaries now act on all colours that contain them, so lowering blue saturation also
  softens warm tones, and several sliders together no longer pile up. Calibration now acts on the
  white balanced picture, and the shadow tint darkens slightly as it tints. Pictures you already
  edited with camera calibration, and the setting that adapts colours to the camera model, may
  look different.

- **Strong white balance keeps bright areas clean:** on raw photos, white balance and camera
  calibration now act before the tone curve, so a strong warm or cool setting no longer tints
  bright areas fully and presets with their own white balance look closer to how they were
  made. Pictures you already edited with a changed white balance keep their look.

- **Waiting indicator while the picture is computed:** removing a plain background, and applying
  a preset, LUT or filter, now show a progress indicator on the picture until the result is
  ready, instead of looking as if nothing happened. While presets are computed you can still
  pick the next one.

- **Hiding the photo shows transparency right away:** after hiding the photo in the layers panel,
  the empty areas showed black until the next change. They now show the transparency background
  at once.

- **Clearer graphics card check:** after a successful check, the performance settings now say
  plainly that image editing uses the graphics card. On a Mac with an Apple chip, the card shows
  up with the chip's name as a built-in graphics unit instead of a number.

- **No more jagged edges around coloured stage light with presets:** presets that tint the
  shadows, such as a teal look, could leave a hard, jagged edge and a green fringe where red stage
  light fades into the dark. The light now fades out smoothly.

- **Presets only once in the list:** importing the same XMP preset or LUT again, even from
  another folder or under another name, no longer adds a second tile. Duplicates already in the
  list are removed once.

- **Camera, date and location for Huawei HEIC photos:** HEIC pictures from Huawei phones now show
  their camera, capture date and location in the info panel.

- **Loading a folder of presets or LUTs:** a large folder no longer freezes the window. A progress
  bar shows while it is read.

- **Canon EOS R8 Mark II colours:** its RAW files were developed as if shot in daylight, because
  the camera's white balance was not read. They now use the white balance set in the camera.

- **Canon EOS R6 brightness:** with the brightness matched to the camera model, its RAW files
  were developed brighter than other cameras. The R6 now gets its own measured value like every
  other model, so unedited pictures start a little darker.

- **Soft transitions in coloured stage light:** where strongly coloured light blew out skin or
  clothing, the bright area had a hard edge against the coloured light around it and looked
  washed out orange. RAW files are now developed with more room for strong colours, so the light
  fades smoothly into the bright area.

- **More natural strong colours:** RAW files keep strong colours such as stage light, flowers
  and saturated clothing intact further into the development, so they come out closer to what
  you saw, with smoother gradations.

- **Converted DNG files no longer too bright:** a DNG made from another RAW file with a converter
  or another photo program often started brighter than the original RAW. It now develops like
  the original.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.71-4
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.71


### What's new

- **Fujifilm lens corrections from the camera:** when the lens database has no profile for your
  Fujifilm lens, FerrumPix now corrects its distortion and vignetting with the values the camera
  stores in the RAF file, as it already did for distortion with Sony, Olympus and Panasonic.

- **More processor cores for the models:** a new setting under Performance decides how many
  processor cores denoising and the other models may use. By default it is still half of them, so
  the app stays responsive; more cores make the models faster when they run on the processor.

- **Copy and paste adjustments in the gallery:** right click an edited RAW or PSD and choose
  Adjustments, Copy adjustments, then paste them onto a whole selection. It uses the same clipboard as copy and
  paste in the editor, so you can copy in one place and paste in the other. RAW and PSD files
  get the adjustments in their sidecar file; JPG, PNG and WebP are overwritten after asking.

- **Detail sliders named and grouped as in the reference program:** the luminance noise reduction,
  formerly Smoothing in the Blur group, now sits as Luminance with its Detail and Method in the
  renamed Noise Reduction group, next to Color, and sharpening is Strength, Radius, Detail and
  Masking. Color there only removes color noise now. Adding noise and color noise moved to the
  Grain group as the Noise and Color noise sliders, together with Dust/scratches, which now
  only adds and goes further at its maximum. Blur has no group of its own any more and sits in
  Details. Vignette moved to the Details tool below Sharpen, Depth blur to the Effects tool below
  Threshold, and Frame now opens the Effects tool above Grain. The rarely useful Color blotches and Blotch size sliders and the negative halves of
  Noise and Dust/scratches are gone; pictures edited with them keep their look.

- **Whites and Blacks keep the colours:** lowering Whites or raising Blacks no longer drains colour
  from bright areas and midtones; the colours now stay as strong as in the reference program.
  Pictures that use these sliders look a little more colourful than before.

- **Histogram next to the sliders by default:** the analysis graph now sits above the adjustment
  sliders from the start, as Histogram in Adjust, RGB parade in Color and Waveform in Details and
  Effects. Switching it in a tool is remembered as before, and Settings can turn it off. It is
  also switched on once after the update, so if you had turned it off before, turn it off again.

- **Display profiles on Windows and Linux:** in Settings you can choose an ICC profile for each
  connected display, for example from a calibration. Photos in the viewer and editor are then
  shown correctly on the display the window is on, also on wide gamut monitors. Leave it empty
  where the system already does this, such as KDE Plasma with a color profile set.

- **Shorter context menu:** applying, copying and pasting adjustments and the watermark now sit
  together in an Adjustments submenu, rejecting and the series entries in a Sort out submenu. When
  only one of them is available, it stays in the main menu.

- **One graphics card for everything on Linux:** on laptops with two graphics cards, the card you
  choose in Settings under Performance is now used for image editing as well, not only for the
  models. It takes effect after a restart, and the window is then drawn on that card too. The
  same choice is also offered when a model is downloaded, next to the option to use the card.

- **Naming people photo by photo:** the People tab in the sidebar now stays open while you flip
  through your photos, also on photos without faces. Names the recognition filled in on its own
  are shown in italics with a check mark next to them; click it or press ENTER to confirm the
  name, so you can see at a glance which photos you have already been through. TAB moves from
  name to name, and after the last one straight to the first name in the next photo.

- **Stacks on and off from the gallery:** a button in the gallery footer, next to the selection
  buttons, turns the stacking of bursts and RAW+JPEG pairs on and off. It is the same setting as
  in Settings, so both always show the same state.

- **Sharpening and colour noise reduction like the reference:** sharpening now works on brightness
  only, so it no longer strengthens colour fringes and colour noise, and strong edges get smaller
  halos. Colour noise reduction measures the noise in each picture and removes only that, instead
  of washing out real colour. Both were matched against renders of the reference program, so
  presets with sharpening and noise reduction come out much closer. Pictures that already use
  sharpening or colour noise reduction will look somewhat different.

- **No more jagged edges and speckles from the colour mixer:** colour noise reduction now runs
  before all colour and tone adjustments, and the colour mixer no longer changes the brightness of
  nearly grey, noisy shadows. Presets that treat neighbouring colours very differently left jagged
  edges around coloured lights and speckles on calm surfaces.

- **Calmer colours with presets that use the colour mixer:** neighbouring colour bands now blend
  smoothly into each other, and the colour mixer decides on a slightly smoothed colour which band
  a pixel belongs to. Presets that treat two neighbouring colours very differently left blotchy,
  speckled areas where a colour sits between them, for example on lettering in the background.

- **Sharper colour edges in saved JPEGs:** JPEG files you save or export, and collages, now keep
  the full colour resolution instead of halving it. Coloured edges such as stage lights and text
  stay crisp, the files get about a third larger.

- **More colour in blown highlights:** where a RAW file clipped only some colour channels, for
  example in a bright sky or a lit face, FerrumPix now rebuilds the missing channel from the others
  and from the colours around it. Pulling down exposure or highlights brings back more natural
  colour there instead of flat white, while bright lamps and the sun stay neutral.

- **Camera calibration closer to the reference:** shadow tint now works across the whole picture
  like in the reference program instead of only in the shadows, where it was far too strong and
  turned red and skin tones. All calibration sliders now have the strength of the reference,
  several of them used together no longer cancel each other out, and together with the curves of
  a preset they no longer push reds too far. The colours matched to each camera model (an option
  in Settings) have been measured again on this basis, for 80 models.

- **True colours under artificial light:** most cameras come with two colour profiles, one for
  daylight and one for warm tungsten light. FerrumPix now blends between them according to the
  white balance of each RAW file, as the reference program does, instead of always using the
  daylight one. Photos under tungsten, stage or other warm light come out with clearly more
  accurate colours, daylight photos change only slightly. The colour temperature shown for a RAW
  file is calculated the same way and can differ a little from before.

- **Preset amount:** after applying an XMP preset, an Amount slider appears in the preset panel.
  0 % is the picture without the preset, 100 % the preset and 200 % its changes twice. It goes
  away with the next edit, as in the reference program.

- **Presets with colour curves apply completely:** presets that combine red, green and blue curves
  with a tone curve, about a third of common presets, used to leave out their tone sliders, colour
  mixer, calibration, sharpening and noise reduction. They now apply in full and come out clearly
  closer to the reference program. Colour curves without a tone curve are ignored there, and now
  here as well.

- **Starting values for sharpening and noise:** a RAW without edits now starts with sharpening 40
  and colour noise reduction 25, like in the reference program. In Settings you can change these
  starting values and set one for noise reduction as well. Resetting all edits returns to them.
  A colour noise starting value of 0 is raised to 25 once after the update; set it back to 0 if
  you chose that on purpose.

- **Whole pictures in the gallery grid:** a new setting shows each picture complete in its tile,
  portrait or landscape, instead of cropping it to the tile.

- **Sensor border removed by default:** RAW files now start without the thin strip of unusable
  pixels at the edge of the sensor, in the gallery, the viewer and the editor. You can switch it
  off for a single picture under lens correction. Pictures you have already edited stay as they
  were.

- **Search a single photo for people:** when a photo has never been searched for faces, the People
  tab in the sidebar now says so and offers a button that searches just this photo. The message
  that nobody was recognised only appears once the photo has actually been searched.

- **People in RAW and HEIC photos:** face recognition now also finds people in RAW files, using
  the picture the camera embedded in them, and in HEIC, JPEG XL, TIFF and PSD files. Before, these
  photos were skipped without a word. Faces in RAW files also show their thumbnails in the sidebar
  and are written to the sidecar file like those in JPEGs. Photos in these formats are searched
  again the next time you search for faces. A RAW with the JPEG the camera saved next to it counts
  as one photo for a person.

- **Undo a reject from the tile:** clicking the red reject badge on a gallery tile takes back the
  reject for that photo.

- **Settings open faster:** the settings page is now prepared bit by bit while you are not using
  the app, so opening it for the first time is as quick as every time after.

### Fixes

- **Old Canon RAW files no longer come out yellow:** CRW files from cameras such as the
  PowerShot G3, G5, G6, S50, S70, Pro1 and EOS D30 that were shot with automatic white balance
  were developed as if in daylight, so pictures taken under indoor light looked deep yellow.
  FerrumPix now works out the white balance from the picture for them.

- **Raising the exposure of a RAW no longer flashes strong colours too bright:** until the
  picture was rebuilt in the background, strongly coloured areas looked brighter than afterwards.

- **Gallery tiles update after a batch:** after pasting or applying adjustments to RAW and PSD
  files, the tiles kept showing the old picture without the edited badge until they were reloaded.
  They now update right away.

- **Saving your own gradient presets:** a gradient saved as a preset in the fill settings did not
  appear in the list. It is now saved and can be removed again with the bin next to the list.

- **Display profiles on KDE Plasma:** the settings could say that no displays were found until
  the window was moved once. The displays are now listed as soon as the settings open.

- **Less memory over long sessions:** FerrumPix no longer keeps the full metadata of every
  picture it has ever read. With large watched folders this used to add up to a lot of memory.

- **When deleting fails, the picture stays:** if a picture cannot be deleted, for example because
  the trash is not available, the viewer, the editor and the search results keep showing it
  instead of acting as if it were gone.

- **Graphics card on macOS:** the graphics card option now works on Macs as well. Before, it
  always fell back to the processor there, with an untranslated reason in the settings. When the
  card cannot be used, the settings now give the reason in your language.

- **Phone RAWs no longer have dark corners:** DNG files from phones such as Google Pixel, Xiaomi
  and Nokia or Microsoft Lumia carry a correction for the lens's shading. FerrumPix now applies it,
  so their corners are no longer up to two stops too dark.

- **Files that differ only in upper and lower case:** on Linux, IMG.JPG and IMG.jpg
  in the same folder are now always treated as two pictures. Before, deleting both removed only
  one, the gallery could fail to show new ones, and the viewer and editor could jump to or drop
  the wrong one.

- **Faster browsing of RAW files in the viewer:** when the viewer develops RAW files, moving on
  to the next picture now stops the development of the previous one instead of waiting for it to
  finish.

- **Closed eye in the adjustment groups easier to see:** while a group is hidden for comparison,
  its closed eye now uses the text colour, which stands out on every theme, including the grey
  ones.

- **Film negatives without a colour cast from grain:** on grainy colour negatives, the grain of
  the scan could decide the inversion and tint the whole picture, more so on a large monitor.
  FerrumPix now measures the film so that the grain no longer counts, and the same scan turns out
  the same on every screen.

- **Readable with the yellow accent:** text and icons on accent coloured areas were white on
  yellow, for example on the selected layer, the badges on gallery tiles, the drop hints and the
  tick in checkboxes. They now turn dark whenever white would not stand out.

- **Soft Light blending corrected:** over dark areas, layers and PSD files in Soft Light came out
  too light. Pictures that use Soft Light can look a little darker there than before.

- **More LUT files work:** .cube files with a 1D curve in front of the 3D table, pure 1D LUTs and
  LUTs with their own input range used to have no effect at all. They are now applied as the file
  describes.

- **XMP presets with the profile written in another form:** the profile and its amount were lost
  when a preset stored them as separate entries instead of attributes. Both forms are now read.

- **Automatic perspective correction only where lines really converge:** a single slanted edge,
  branches or other edges in the picture could make it tilt photos without any architecture, often
  as far as it goes. It now only corrects when most edges run towards a common vanishing point,
  and leaves the rest alone.

- **Tooltips in the adjustment groups translated:** the tooltips of the compare and reset buttons
  in the group headers sometimes appeared in German, for example in Colour, Colour mixer and
  Colour grading.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.70
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.70


### What's new

- **Straight to the editor from the "edited" badge.** A click on the badge of an edited picture
  in the gallery opens it in the editor.

- **Text stays text in PSD exports.** Plain text now goes into the PSD as a real text layer, so
  the wording, font and size can still be changed in other editors. Text with a shadow, glow,
  outline, gradient or along a path still goes out as an image. Opened again in FerrumPix, the
  text comes back as text in the right place, even after cropping. Text layers from other
  programs now also keep their angle, alignment and letter spacing when you open them as text.

- **Locked layers stay locked in PSD files.** Locking a layer's position or its transparent
  pixels now carries over to the PSD and back, also for the bottom layer.

- **Smoother sliders in the editor.** The short freeze when you first grab a slider on a large
  picture is gone, and the picture follows the slider more closely. When zoomed in, the sharp
  detail view no longer keeps recalculating in the background while you drag; it appears as soon
  as you hold still. Histogram and tone curve are now updated in the background, and dragging
  highlights, shadows, whites, blacks or vibrance is noticeably quicker.

- **Graphics card for image editing (try it out).** A new switch under Settings, Performance lets
  the graphics card calculate colour and tones as well as all detail and effect tools such as
  noise reduction, sharpening, clarity, haze, blur, grain and vignette, in the preview as well as
  for export and batch processing. Sliders react noticeably faster on large pictures, and
  sharpening with the deconvolution method no longer takes seconds. It is off by default; when you
  turn it on, FerrumPix first checks that the card calculates the same picture as the processor
  and otherwise stays with the processor. Curves, colour grading, point colour and LUTs are
  included. Without a real graphics card, for example in a virtual machine, with a graphics card
  that turns out slower than the processor, and after the graphics driver hung or crashed,
  FerrumPix also stays with the processor.

- **Immich and Nextcloud photos on the map.** The map view now also shows pictures from a
  connected Immich or Nextcloud server, using the location the server knows for them. For
  Nextcloud this needs version 28 or newer.

- **Developed RAWs are marked in the viewer too.** As in the editor, the file name at the top of
  the window turns to the accent colour when the viewer shows a RAW developed by FerrumPix rather
  than the camera's built-in preview.

- **Smaller fixes:** invisible layers no longer turn into empty full-size layers in a PSD export,
  and PSD files open a little faster. The last page of the Windows installer now reads
  "Launch FerrumPix" in English instead of the German wording.

### Fixes

- **Exposure no longer jumps after you let go:** when you change the exposure of a RAW, the
  picture no longer shifts in the shadows, highlights or strong colours a moment after you release
  the slider. Only very bright pictures can still gain some highlight detail at that moment. The
  exposure slider also follows the mouse like the other sliders instead of lagging behind it.

- **White stays white in the colour mixer:** lowering the luminance of a colour such as yellow
  or green no longer tints bright clouds, white walls or blown highlights.

- **Collage layout buttons:** the selected layout is highlighted again. Before, "Grid" stayed
  highlighted, and with "Hero" the hint and the choice of the hero position did not appear.
  
- **Batch rename:** the placeholder buttons now sit in a tidy row under the name pattern, as in
  the export dialog.
  
- **Histogram, waveform and RGB parade in the editor** now show the whole picture including its
  layers and objects. With layered PSD files they stayed empty.
  
- **Faster browsing of developed RAWs in the viewer:** when you skip quickly through RAW files with
  development switched on, the viewer no longer develops the pictures you have already passed.
  
- **RAWs open faster in the editor from the viewer:** while a RAW stays on screen in the viewer,
  FerrumPix prepares it in the background, so switching to the editor takes noticeably less time.
  
- **Vibrance protects skin tones:** raising Vibrance now holds back on reds, oranges and skin
  while lifting greens, blues and skies more, and it no longer brightens colours as it saturates
  them. Before, it acted almost like Saturation. It is also gentler overall now, especially on
  faces, so skin no longer turns orange at high settings.
  
- **ISO on Nikon JPGs:** pictures taken at the extended Hi ISO settings now show their ISO in the
  gallery and the info panel. Before, only the NEF files had it.
  
- **Opening PSD files:** empty layers are kept as empty paint layers with their name and mask
  instead of disappearing. Text that is skewed or mirrored now comes in as an image, so it keeps
  its look instead of turning into straight text.
  
- **Tone curve on a layer:** when you adjust a layer, the histogram behind the curve now shows
  that layer instead of the background, so it no longer stays empty with layered PSD files.
  
- **Face names from other photo programs:** named faces that another program stored in an XMP
  sidecar file now come into FerrumPix with their name and position. Before, files in the common
  notation of these programs were skipped.
  
- **Collages with many pictures react much faster:** picture objects are kept in memory instead
  of being read from disk every time, and objects with blend modes like Soft Light are drawn
  several times faster. Moving an object in a collage of 30 pictures no longer takes seconds.
  
- **Clean picture edges:** noise reduction, colour noise reduction, structure, glow, the soft
  filter and sharpening no longer darken the border of the picture or make it slightly
  transparent. With colour noise reduction the colours at the border no longer shift either.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.69
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.69


### What's new

- **See and find your edited pictures.** A new "Edited" section in the gallery filter shows only
  edited or only unedited pictures, so you can select them all and export, convert or upload
  just those. If you like, a small badge on the tile marks edited pictures, next to the one for
  rejected pictures; switch it on in the settings under "Mark edited photos". In the photo wall
  it only appears while the mouse is over the tile. Stars, labels and keywords alone don't count
  as an edit.

- **Sharper lens correction.** Correcting lens distortion no longer softens fine detail such as
  hair; pictures keep noticeably more of their sharpness. The lens data is updated as well and
  knows a few more lenses.

- **The random collage looks like a pile of real prints.** Each picture now lies on a white
  print with a soft shadow, keeps its own shape instead of being cut square, and the prints are
  scattered and turned across the whole page and beyond its edges, without gaps in between.
  The picture frame setting sets the width of the white border. You choose how big the prints
  are and how much their sizes vary, and with the margin whether the pile stays inside the page
  or runs over its edges.

- **Collages in any size.** Besides the automatic height, a collage can now take an aspect
  ratio such as 3:2, 16:9 or A4, upright or across, or a width and height of your own.

- **Faster, larger previews for collage and printing.** Both dialogs now read each picture only
  once while they are open instead of again after every change, and they grow with the window
  so the preview gets more room.

- **PSD files open more faithfully.** Layers set to Linear Dodge or Soft Light now blend as they
  should, a painted layer mask next to a vector mask is kept, text, shape and smart object layers no
  longer get their edges masked twice, and one unreadable layer no longer turns the whole file
  flat. When a file uses layer effects such as shadows or strokes, FerrumPix asks whether to
  open it as layers without the effects or as a flattened image. In the gallery and viewer,
  files saved without maximum compatibility no longer show a white area, transparent edges no
  longer get a light fringe, and a saved selection is no longer taken for transparency. PSD
  files exported from FerrumPix store their transparent edges the way other programs expect.
  Combining distant or feathered masks now respects the import's memory limit.

- **Exposure on raw files works like in a raw developer.** The exposure slider now acts on the
  raw data before the tone curve, so darkening brings back detail in bright skies instead of just
  greying them, and brightening opens up the shadows more naturally. While you drag, the picture
  follows at once and already looks almost like the result; a moment after you let go, it is
  rebuilt from the raw data. Automatic enhancement chooses the exposure the same way and gives
  the same result however often you press it.

- **Raw files from every camera come out at the right brightness.** On a new installation,
  FerrumPix now adjusts the base brightness to the camera model from the start, so raw files
  from most cameras no longer open noticeably too bright. If you already use FerrumPix, nothing
  changes for you and your edited pictures keep their look; you can switch it on in the settings
  under "Match base brightness to the camera model".

- **Tone sliders recalibrated.** Shadows, whites, highlights and blacks were tuned again to the
  corrected base brightness. The whites slider now has the strength you would expect in both
  directions, highlights are a little gentler and pulling the blacks down works more strongly.
  The shadows slider now also looks at how much of the picture is bright: next to a bright sky
  or a light wall, dark parts open up further, as in a raw developer. In dark pictures, such as
  concerts or night shots, the highlights slider now pulls bright areas down much more firmly.
  Detail in bright skies and clouds is now always brought back from the raw data, so the
  checkbox for it in the light panel is gone. On raw files, pulling the highlights down now
  reaches into that detail as well: bright skies, clouds and burnt out areas come down about as
  far as in a raw developer, where before the slider stopped at half the way. Clouds and bright
  skies also keep their texture when you pull the highlights down, instead of turning flat and
  milky, and colours there no longer fade. Lifting the shadows keeps their colour as well.
  All pictures now share one calculation for these sliders, so pictures you edited in earlier
  versions can look slightly different.
  
### Fixes
  
- **Smaller fixes.** The text cursor sits in the right place and at the right size, also while
  you resize a text box. The curve editor draws the luminance curve the way it is applied. A
  picture you rename stays in the open burst. Choosing a folder in "Save as", in searches and in
  the settings starts in the folder already entered instead of your home folder. In the filter
  menu, bursts, rejected and edited pictures now come after the colour labels, and the people
  and places lists are as tall as the keyword list.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.68
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.68


### What's new

- **Depth fog reaches the foreground.** A new Foreground slider in Depth fog puts some fog over
  the nearest parts of the picture too, so a person or an animal close to the camera no longer
  stays perfectly clear while everything behind them disappears in the mist.

- **File names in the photo wall.** The photo wall has no caption strip under its tiles, so a raw
  file and its .fpx project looked the same. Hovering over a tile now shows its name with the
  extension and the details you would otherwise see under it, in the same info box the EXIF and
  XMP badges use.

- **The eyedropper shows what it hits.** A small label follows the eyedropper over the picture
  with a swatch and the value of the color under its tip.

- **File name placeholders with the time.** Batch rename has two more placeholders to click
  that insert the file date and the date taken together with the time of day. The file name
  field of the other batch dialogs now offers the same placeholders to click.

- **Batch rename resolves name conflicts.** If two pictures would get the same name, or the
  name is already taken in the folder, the next one gets _1, _2 and so on instead of stopping
  the rename.

- **File extensions in lower case.** Saving under a new name, exporting, batch converting,
  renaming and batch renaming now write the file extension in lower case, so IMG_0001.JPG
  becomes IMG_0001.jpg. Files saved in place keep their name.

- **Highlights and shadows keep their detail.** Both sliders now work on the brightness of the
  surroundings instead of each single pixel: pulling the highlights down brings out the
  structure in a bright sky instead of flattening it, and lifting the shadows does the same in
  dark corners.

- **Whites adapt to the picture.** The whites slider now looks at how close the brightest parts
  already are to white. A flat picture opens up further, one whose highlights already reach
  white is lifted more gently, so the slider behaves much more like you would expect from a raw
  editor. Highlights, shadows and whites also read a film negative as the positive you see.

- **Raw files from every camera come out at the right brightness.** On a new installation,
  FerrumPix now adjusts the base brightness to the camera model from the start, so raw files
  from most cameras no longer open noticeably too bright. If you already use FerrumPix, 
  you can switch it on in the settings under "Match base brightness to the camera model".

### Fixes

- Context menus and footer menus always open at the size of their content and from the top:
  no more changing sizes, missing rows or scroll arrows when the menu fits on the screen.
  The folder tree menu no longer shows doubled or trailing separator lines, and the dialogs for
  setting the capture date and the place are wide enough for their options.

- Picking exactly black, white, red or another standard color in a color picker no longer
  falls back to a different color. This affected the background of a new document, of a
  collage and behind transparent areas, the replace color brush and the gradient map. Edits
  and settings saved earlier with such a color show it correctly again.

- A rating, label or keyword on a RAW or PSD no longer replaces an edit file that could not be
  read, for example one from a newer version or on a drive that is offline; the same goes for
  rotating in the viewer and applying adjustments to a selection. The change stays in the
  catalog and the gallery says so.

- Overwriting a file or folder while pasting or moving keeps the old one until the new one is
  complete. If the copy fails, for example because a network drive drops out, the old file or
  folder is back as it was. Replacing a folder no longer takes along the sidecar of a photo
  that happens to have the same name. If the old version cannot be removed afterwards, the
  window says where it was left.

- Saving a JPEG, PNG or WebP with its photo information no longer reports success when that
  information could not be carried over. The file stays as it was and the save is shown as
  failed. This now also covers rotating in the viewer, batch changes and replacing a picture on
  a server, even when the drive drops out in the middle of reading.

- Converting RAW files to DNG over an existing DNG no longer leaves a half written file behind
  when the conversion fails or is cancelled. The existing DNG stays as it was.

- Pasting, moving and converting to DNG no longer fail for files with very long names.

- An adjustment stacked above an object now updates right away when the object changes
  elsewhere in the picture, instead of only after the next full refresh.

- Saved searches, favorites and settings that could not be written are now reported in the
  gallery instead of silently counting as saved. A removed saved search no longer comes back
  after a restart, and a favorite that could not be stored is no longer reported as already
  present.

- XMP sidecar files from other programs now travel along when a picture is renamed, copied,
  moved or deleted, so ratings, keywords and edits are found at the new place. A shared
  photo.xmp stays where another file with the same name still needs it.

- When a sidecar cannot be moved to the trash or deleted, the remaining file is reported.
  Renaming a picture whose sidecar stays behind no longer says the rename failed: the picture
  is renamed, and the sidecar is named in the warning bar. The same warning no longer appears
  twice when a batch runs again over the same files.

- Objects with their own highlights, shadows or whites in a saved .fpx or edit file look the
  same as when they were saved. A thin object, or one that reaches over the edge of the
  picture, now looks the same while editing and after saving.

- Moving a folder to the trash no longer takes along the sidecar of a photo next to it that
  has the same name as the folder.

- Some NEF files from the Nikon Z50II and Z5II that could not be decoded showed colored noise
  and a green area. They now show the preview embedded in the file instead.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.67
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.67


### What's new

- **Point color.** In the color mixer, a second view picks a color in the photo with the
  eyedropper and shifts only that color in hue, saturation and luminance, with a range for how
  far around it other colors are affected. Up to eight colors, shown as circles; "Show range"
  greys out everything a color does not reach. Presets with point color now arrive complete.

- **Colored sliders.** A new setting shows sliders with a color meaning as a color gradient,
  such as temperature, tint, the color mixer, calibration, the channel mixer and point color.
  Off by default.

- **The eye of a group works on layers too.** It hides the group's adjustments of the selected
  layer or correction layer for a moment and brings them back.

- **Tilt-shift.** A new group in Effects keeps a band through the picture sharp and blurs more
  and more towards the edges, like a tilted lens. Width, transition, angle and position of the
  band can be set, and the group can be hidden or moved in the settings like any other.

- **Depth fog.** Another new group in Effects lays fog over the picture by distance: near things
  stay clear, far things fade into the fog colour. Like depth blur it needs the depth model and is
  applied into the pixels with its own button.

- **Missing models are offered where they are needed.** A function that needs a model which is
  not downloaded yet now asks whether to download it when you try to use it, instead of being
  greyed out. Only the file that function needs is fetched, and the same window shows the progress.
  Where the model can use the graphics card and acceleration is off, it offers to switch it on,
  checks the card and shows the result.

- **The graphics card check is remembered.** Settings no longer show a card as unchecked after
  every restart; each new check replaces the result.

### Fixes

- The reset button of a group works on a selected layer right away instead of only after the
  layer is deselected.

- The eyedropper works on a selected layer: the click no longer starts moving the layer, and the
  point color takes the color of the layer instead of the photo below it.

- After undo, redo or the eye of a group, the sliders of Details, Noise and some of Sharpness
  stayed where they were, although the picture already showed the restored values. They follow
  now.

- The reset button and the eye of an adjustment group only touch that group's own sliders. Details
  also reset the noise sliders, and the reset button of Vignette reset the grain and the lens
  corrections as well.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.66
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.66


### What's new

- **RAW development on macOS without Homebrew.** The Mac packages now bring their own LibRaw, so
  RAW files are developed from the sensor data even if nothing is installed. A LibRaw from
  Homebrew is still preferred when it is there.

- **Compare a single curve.** Right-click RGB, R, G, B or L above the tone curve to set that
  channel's curve back to a straight line for a moment; the next right-click brings it back,
  just like comparing a single slider.

- **Compare a whole group.** The eye next to the reset button of Light, Color, Tone curve,
  Color mixer, Colour grading, Calibration, Channel Mixer, Gradient Map, Posterize, Threshold,
  Sharpness, Blur, Noise, Details, Vignette and Grain hides that group's adjustments for a
  moment, so you see the photo without them; click it again to bring them back.

### Fixes

- Moving the temperature of a RAW photo no longer throws away the tint of the shot. Even a small
  nudge could tip the whole picture towards green or magenta, most visibly on phone photos; the
  same happened with automatic enhancement, the white balance picker and presets that shift the
  white balance. The tint row now shows the tint of the shot, just as the temperature row shows its
  temperature, and a double-click brings both back.

- The tooltip of the button that leads from a burst back to its folder is translated now.

- Enlarging the canvas no longer makes the photo shrink inside the editor. Even one extra pixel
  could show the picture at half its size with a huge border around it; the saved image was
  always right, now the editor shows the same.

- Scans saved as TIFF or DNG are read far less often: reading their details no longer loads the
  whole file, so indexing watched folders, opening a picture in the editor and the info panel are
  much quicker on a network drive. A film scan as DNG used to travel over the network up to four
  times, now about once.

- The Microsoft Store version no longer looks for a newer version on GitHub; updates come through
  the Store.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.65
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.65


### What's new

- **Compare a single slider.** Right-click a slider or its number field in the editor to set it
  to its default for a moment; slider and field change colour, and the next right-click brings
  your value back. Several sliders can be compared at once, and in the number field SPACE does
  the same. Saving while comparing saves what you see, and before you move to another picture
  every slider gets its value back.

- **More cameras with their own base brightness.** Thirty more camera models, among them the
  Canon EOS 77D and M5, Fujifilm X-T2 and GFX 50S, Panasonic G9, Pentax K-3 Mark III and KP and
  several Sony Alpha models, now have their own value for the setting that matches the base
  brightness to the camera, and the Fujifilm X-T30 II has its own colours.

- **More from blown highlights.** Recovering highlights from the raw data now brings back more
  detail in bright skies, pink spots in recovered highlights turn neutral, and when you brighten
  a picture and pull the highlights down, recovered clouds keep their structure.

- **Faster detail sliders.** Sharpening, noise reduction, clarity, haze, vignette and the other
  detail and effect sliders respond faster, because the light and colour work underneath them is
  kept instead of being worked out again.

- **Lens correction for Sigma, Tamron and Tokina lenses on Canon.** Canon cameras store only the
  focal length for these lenses; FerrumPix now works out the lens from the camera's lens number,
  focal range and aperture, so the Tamron 17-50 and 18-200, the Sigma 10-20 and many more are
  recognised. Where the lens cannot be told apart, the correction for a Canon lens of the same
  focal length is no longer applied by mistake.

### Fixes

- Switching to another picture while depth blur was set but not applied no longer leaves the
  old picture's blurred preview over the new one.

- Bright, almost white areas in RAW files, such as lit fluorescent tubes or a sunny patch, no
  longer turn pink, also without recovering highlights.

- A RAW saved as JPEG, PNG or another format keeps the name of its lens, also where the camera
  stores the lens only in its own data.

- Copying, moving, duplicating or dragging a burst takes all of its pictures along, and a tag
  set on a burst reaches every picture in it; the white balance menu keeps its choice through
  undo and in saved edits.

- Scans saved as TIFF or DNG are read far less often: reading their details no longer loads the
  whole file, so indexing watched folders, opening a picture in the editor and the info panel are
  much quicker on a network drive. A film scan as DNG used to travel over the network up to four
  times, now about once.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.64
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.64


### What's new

- **Lens correction for compact cameras.** RAW files from cameras with a built-in lens, such as
  the Panasonic LX and FZ, Canon PowerShot, Sony RX and Fujifilm X100 series, are now corrected
  for distortion, coloured fringes and vignetting.

- **Lens correction from the camera's own data.** Sony, Olympus, OM System and Panasonic cameras
  store their distortion correction, most of them also their colour fringe correction, in the RAW
  file. Where the lens database has no profile, FerrumPix now uses
  that data, and the lens panel says so.

- **Vignetting follows the focus distance.** Where the camera records how far it was focused,
  the edge darkening is corrected for that distance instead of always for infinity, which helps
  close-ups in particular.

- **A real blur.** The Blur group now has a slider that softens the whole picture evenly, from a
  gentle touch to a strong blur, and it looks the same in the preview as in the export. The
  slider that used to be called Blur is now called Smoothing, because that is what it does: it
  reduces noise and leaves edges and detail alone.

- **Recalibrated sliders.** Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Vibrance, the
  luminance of the colour mixer, the brightness in colour grading and the vignette now have a
  more natural strength and range. Colour grading tints more evenly, the colour mixer bands sit
  where presets expect them, and tone and channel curves shape colours the way presets were made
  for, so presets with curves no longer drift red or green. Highlights and Shadows also take the
  brightness of the whole picture into account: in a bright picture Shadows open up dark areas
  further, in a dark one they stay gentler. 

### Fixes

- **Highlights, Shadows, Whites and Blacks no longer turn tones around.** Pulling highlights
  down and shadows up together, especially at full strength, could make the midtones run
  backwards; brighter parts of a gradient came out darker than the parts next to them. Strong
  settings also keep colours on their hue now, so an orange stays orange instead of turning a
  greyish yellow.

- **More lenses are recognised.** Older Canon EOS, Olympus Four Thirds and Panasonic G bodies,
  Samsung NX, Sony A-mount and Pentax cameras, including Pentax DNG files, now name the lens they
  were used with, so lens correction finds its profile. A Leica DG lens no longer gets the profile of a Lumix lens of the same range.

- **Two single shots in the same second are no longer shown as a burst** when the camera recorded
  them as single shots.

- **Nikon lenses are recognised by name.** FerrumPix now knows about 600 Nikon F lenses, including
  many Sigma, Tamron and Tokina models, instead of guessing from focal length and aperture. Lens
  correction no longer mixes up an AF-S with an AF-P zoom, an autofocus 50 mm with a manual one, or
  a Sigma with the Nikon lens of the same range.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.63
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.63


### What's new

- **Bursts and RAW+JPEG pairs as stacks.** When switched on in Settings, shots taken in quick
  succession and the camera JPEG next to a RAW appear as one thumbnail. A click on a burst shows
  just that burst until you go back to the folder; pictures of a burst are deleted there one at a
  time, never the whole burst at once. The navigation buttons only leave the burst view and stay
  in the folder. Ratings, labels, keywords and deleting on a pair apply to both files.

- **Sharpest shot first.** Within a burst the sharpest shot moves to the front, and each shot shows
  how sharp it is compared to the best one.

- **Reject while culling.** X marks pictures as rejected, SHIFT+X rejects everything in a burst
  except the chosen shot. Rejected pictures are dimmed and can be hidden or shown on their own with
  the filter; the mark is written to the sidecar as well.

- **File operations outside the home folder.** A new setting allows copying, moving, renaming and
  deleting on other drives, mounted media and network folders. It is off by default, and system
  folders stay locked either way.

- **Eight editable looks in Filters.** Base Light, Color Harmony and Luminous Curve highlight
  individual adjustment groups; Desert Light, Film Grain, Color Haze, Clear View and Timeless
  offer further starting points. Every look consists only of ordinary FerrumPix sliders,
  HSL settings, curves, grain and vignette, so it remains fully editable after applying it and is
  also available in batch adjustments and Export to.

- **A clearer editor footer.** The output dimensions no longer compete with the centered zoom
  controls on smaller windows.

- **Accent-colored window logo.** The “Pix” part of the title-bar logo now follows the selected
  accent color and strength.

### Fixes

- **Stars, heart and metadata badges on thumbnails now sit on one line**, the heart has the same
  color as the stars, and the smallest thumbnail size leaves room for every badge.

- **Missing translations filled in:** the rename and convert dialogs, the window button setting,
  the watermark offsets and the shape names in the editor.

- **Color grading now tones black-and-white pictures.** Before, the black-and-white look turned
  every toning back into gray.

- **The viewer comparison no longer puts a picture next to itself.** Paging skips the pinned
  picture, and it is dimmed in the filmstrip.

- **Lens data below thumbnails now comes from the same actual focal length as the EXIF panel.**
  A 50 mm lens is no longer labelled 75 mm on a crop camera, and existing catalog entries are
  refreshed automatically. This also refreshes missing lens names, including Sigma lenses, and
  lenses added to FerrumPix's lens list later now reach photos that were already catalogued.

- **HSL color chips now refresh their change indicators** when an image is loaded or switched, or
  when global adjustments are reset.

- **More precise size controls.** Frame width and margin, shadow size and glow size can be adjusted
  in 0.1 steps.

- **Mouse-wheel input on numeric fields no longer builds up a delayed queue.** Rapid extra wheel
  impulses are discarded instead of continuing to change the value after scrolling stops.

- The frame group only appears for the main image or the selected frame layer. A small frame
  toggle in the image footer shows whether the frame is active. Frame layers cannot be duplicated
  or copied and pasted, keeping at most one frame layer in a project.

- **More precise numeric controls** are available for tone and color adjustments, color grading,
  detail effects, white balance and layer opacity. Kelvin white balance uses 10 K steps.

- Removing a layer's adjustments while editing that object no longer lets stale adjustment values
  reappear when changing its effects.

- Pasting a copied mask or selection without a selected layer creates a new mask or selection layer.

- Double-clicking an overlay object now opens its matching editing tool; a single click still leaves
  the current adjustment tool active.

- Image text now uses HarfBuzz shaping for Thai and other complex scripts, with shaped widths also
  used for drawing and multiline alignment.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.62
body:
## 0.9.62

### What's new

- **The frame works like the other objects.** It has an on and off switch in its group, and below
  it the same fill, shadow and glow groups as text, with every option: all gradient types with as
  many color stops as you like, presets, and shadow and glow inside or outside. Radial and diamond
  gradients run along the frame itself, so every color shows. The frame can also keep a distance
  from the edge of the picture. A semi-transparent gradient frame now keeps the opacity you set
  instead of turning fainter.

- **Warp beyond the edge.** The grid, envelope and line warps let you drag the corners and edges
  of the picture past its border, like a free transform. The preview shows the part outside
  darkened, and applying keeps the picture size, so what was pulled out is cut off. Edges snap
  back onto their line when you come close, so they stay straight unless you mean otherwise.

### Fixes

- Red eye removal moved to the image brush, next to the eraser, dodge, burn, sponge and replace
  color. One click on the pupil removes the red inside the brush circle. Blur, healing brush and
  clone stamp no longer carry it.

- In the selection tool, fill, stroke, shadow and glow only show once there is a selection or a
  selection layer is picked, since they have nothing to work on before that.

- The size of shadow and glow can now be set to one decimal place, and a new glow starts at size 5
  instead of 10.

- DNG files that store their pictures as JPEG XL now show their large embedded preview instead of
  a tiny thumbnail. Developing their raw data is not possible yet.

- Double-clicking a slider now returns it to its starting value everywhere. Lens correction,
  color grading blend, depth blur, the mask and selection range sliders and two dialog sliders used
  to jump to zero instead. Depth blur now starts at zero strength, the same value its reset uses.

- Raw files from the Fujifilm X100VI get better matched brightness and colors.

- The shadow of the paint brush is visible now. It used to sit almost exactly under the stroke,
  and its softness and size had next to no effect. The brush starts with a larger shadow offset
  and glow size than objects.

- The number fields next to the sliders stand out slightly from the panel, so they are easier to
  spot and click.

- While the eyedropper of a color field hovers over the picture, the color field already shows the
  color under it. It is only taken over with the click.

- A cropped or rotated picture no longer shrinks on the canvas while you drag an adjustment slider.

- Save as, export, apply adjustments and the other dialogs with a target folder remember whether
  you last picked the current or the last folder.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.61
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.61


### What's new

- Four more adjustments that also work on adjustment layers. Under Color, a channel mixer
  mixes each channel anew from red, green and blue, for swapped colors, a cast that one channel is
  missing, or black and white from your own channel mix. A gradient map turns the brightness
  of the picture into a gradient between two colors, for duotone or false color looks. Under
  Effects, posterize reduces each channel to a few flat steps, and threshold turns the
  picture into pure black and white.

- **Stroke a selection.** The selection tool draws a line along the edge of the selection, inside,
  centered or outside, with its own color, width, hardness and round or sharp corners. A selection
  can also cast a shadow and glow, like an object, around the outside while the selected area
  itself stays as it is. Fill, stroke, shadow and glow of a selection are live: tick them on,
  every change shows at once, they come back when the selection layer is picked again, and they can
  be switched off. While an object is selected, its own groups show instead.

- **Fill and stroke work the same everywhere.** Text, watermarks, shapes, symbols and the selection
  share the same fill and stroke groups. A stroke on any object can now sit inside, centered or
  outside, fade out softly and have round or sharp corners. Fill, stroke, shadow and glow switch on
  with a checkbox in their header and only open when they are in use.

- **Gradients with any number of colors.** A fill can be linear, radial, angle, reflected or
  diamond shaped. Click the gradient bar to add a color, drag to move it, drag it off to remove it;
  each color can be partly transparent. Size, center and repeating can be set, and a list of
  ready-made gradients sits next to the bar, where your own can be saved too.

- **Inner shadow and inner glow.** Shadow and glow can lie outside, inside or both. Inside, the
  shadow falls along the inner edge that faces the light and the glow shines from the edge into
  the shape, on objects, text, brush strokes and selections alike.

### Fixes

- Linear and radial fills now show exactly the colors you set: a radial fill reaches its outer
  color at the edge of a circle or text instead of stopping short of it.

- Text and symbols keep the same stroke width whether "Blend the outline too" is on or off.

- Shrinking a picture a lot, such as a full film scan down to a size for the web, no longer turns
  film grain and fine patterns into coarse stripes. This applies to resizing, exporting with a size,
  printing and collages.

- Raw files from more camera models start out closer in brightness and color to what the camera
  intended.

- The status in the editor footer uses the free space up to the zoom buttons instead of cutting
  messages short.

- A text layer selected in another tool stays selected when you switch to the text tool to change
  it, the same for watermarks, pictures and QR codes. "Blend the outline too" can be switched at
  any time and now works for image layers, copied selections and image watermarks as well.

- Exported PSD files carry an sRGB color profile. Before, programs that assume their own working
  space without one could show them too saturated. They also keep the resolution of the original
  and, when metadata is kept, its XMP data such as rating and keywords.

- PSD files in indexed color open, transparent color included, files with more than 300 layers
  keep their layers, and nested groups that some versions write differently no longer fall apart
  into loose layers.

- Lens correction no longer leaves colored streaks in the corners. Where the correction would
  reach past the edge of the picture, it now enlarges the picture just enough to fill the frame,
  in the editor and in the viewer.

- Every step in the history carries its own name. Rotating and flipping the whole picture, the
  perspective sliders, mask density, the feather of a selection, the opacity and visibility of
  adjustment layers and groups, nudging a layer and resetting the lens correction showed up as
  just "Adjustment" before.

- Double-clicking a channel mixer slider returns it to its starting value, 100 on its own channel.

- Shadow and glow no longer show up in every tool after opening a picture while a new object
  was still armed for placing.

- Color buttons in the editor panels sit at the right edge, like the number fields, so a longer
  label such as "Background color" no longer runs into them.

- A group with its checkbox ticked, such as fill, stroke, shadow or glow, stays open, and the
  title in its header lines up with the checkbox and the icon.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.60
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.60


### What's new

- **Any picture can become a layer.** RAW files, PSD, FerrumPix projects, HEIC, JPEG XL and SVG
  can now be added to a picture in the editor as a layer, by dragging them from the filmstrip or a
  file manager, through the insert tool or the filmstrip menu. A RAW comes in developed, with its
  edits if it has any, a PSD or project as its finished picture.

- **Perspective fills the frame on its own.** A new "Fill automatically" option keeps the size
  adjusted while you correct the perspective, so no empty corners are left. When you drag the
  corners in the picture, it fills the frame as you let go.

- **Remove the sensor border.** A new switch under lens correction cuts off the outermost pixel
  rows of a RAW that the sensor does not deliver cleanly and that can show up as colored stripes
  along the edge. It is off by default and offered for more than 300 camera models.

- **Image brush.** The eraser now shares one tool with four new brushes that change the picture
  instead of painting on it: dodge and burn lighten or darken, aimed at the shadows, midtones or
  highlights, the sponge takes color away or adds it, and replace color recolors while keeping
  brightness and texture. They work on the photo and on a selected picture layer.

- **Refine edge.** A new button in the selection tool and in the mask tool makes the edge of a
  selection or mask follow the picture within a narrow band, so hair, fur and fine twigs are picked
  up instead of being cut off hard. It needs no model.

- **Refresh in the folder tree.** Right click a folder and choose "Refresh" to read its subfolders
  again, for example after changes in a file manager. Folders you had opened stay open.

### Fixes

- Lens correction recognises Sigma and Tamron lenses on Canon, Sony and Fujifilm cameras. Before,
  it often picked a lens of the camera maker with similar numbers, and a Sigma 24-70 on a Canon
  was corrected like a Canon 24-70.

- On Nikon cameras many more Sigma, Tamron and Tokina lenses are recognised by name, among them
  the Sigma 17-50mm f/2.8, 35mm and 50mm Art and the Tamron SP 24-70mm, and older bodies such as
  the D40, D200 or D300 now report them too. A Tamron 24-70 is no longer corrected like a Nikon
  24-70.

- Lens correction no longer mixes up lenses with a different focal length or brightness, such as a
  10-20mm zoom taken for a 20mm lens. When no matching lens is known, the photo is left as it is.

- The lens search field also understands input like "Sigma 2.8/17-50", and when nothing matches it
  says so instead of staying silent.

- On Windows the catalog keeps one entry per photo, however its path is spelled. Before, the same
  file could be stored twice, read in again and carry two different ratings. Existing catalogs are
  merged once on the first start.

- The notice that a camera is not supported no longer appears for cameras that are, such as the
  Nikon Z 6II, Z 7II, Z 8, Z 9 and Z f, the OM-1, the Panasonic S5II or phones that save DNG.

- Film negative conversion measures the picture again after cropping. Before, film edges,
  sprocket holes or the scanner holder that were cropped away afterwards still threw off the
  colors. A film base picked with the eyedropper is kept.

- PSD files in 16 and 32 bit open with their layers, as do large PSB files. Before, they
  opened as a single flattened picture. A layer's fill opacity is now taken into account.

- Resetting the effects also takes lens correction back out of the picture. Before, only the
  switches went back while the picture stayed corrected.

- Film negative conversion leaves out the black scanner holder at the edges even without
  cropping. Before, it made the converted picture much too dark.

- Automatic enhancement works on film negatives. Before, it looked at the negative instead of the
  converted picture and pushed it the wrong way, often much too cold and too dark.

- Saving a picture twice in a row with "Save as" keeps retouching, brush strokes, denoising and
  removed objects in the second file too. Before, they were missing there even though the editor
  still showed them. The same applied to saving a project a second time.

- The arrow keys scroll the settings page, as Page Up and Page Down already did.

- On smaller gallery tiles the EXIF, IPTC, XMP and ICC badges no longer sit under the rating stars.
  When there is not enough room for both, only the stars are shown; larger tiles show both.

name: FerrumPix 0.9.59
body:
## What's new in FerrumPix 0.9.59


### What's new

- **Hardness for the clone stamp, healing brush and smudge.** A new hardness slider sets how soft
  or hard the edge of these tools is, just like for the paint brush. It starts where the edge has
  always been, so nothing changes until you move it.

- **Brush sizes are remembered.** The brush, eraser, smudge, healing brush and clone stamp each
  keep their size and hardness when you switch tools, open another picture or restart the app.

- **Histogram, waveform and RGB parade show what you see.** In the gallery and viewer they now
  describe the picture as it is displayed, for RAW files including your edits, the way Lightroom
  does. They also appear much sooner, because the file no longer has to be read a second time.

- **Straighten with a line.** In the Rotate group, press "Draw a line" and drag along an edge in
  the picture that should be level or upright; the picture turns to match. The angle can now be
  set to a hundredth of a degree in the number field, and automatic straightening shows that it
  is working instead of seeming to do nothing.
